title: States of matter
examples: Teacher, what is the difference between a liquid and a gas?
Can you show us what happens when something changes state?
Why do gases spread out so much?

explain.say: Today we learn about the three main states of matter. These are solid, liquid, and gas.
Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: solid, liquid and gas. Look at the solid, the liquid and the gas. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
A solid keeps its shape no matter what container it is in. Think of a rock, for example.
A liquid takes the shape of its container but keeps a certain level. Water in a glass is a good example.
A gas has no fixed shape and no fixed volume. Air around us is a perfect example of a gas.

draw.text: Gas: No fixed shape or volume

explain.say: Particles are tiny bits that make up all matter. In a solid, they are packed tightly together.
Melting is when a solid turns into a liquid. Ice turning into water is a clear example of this.

faq.q: What is the difference between melting and boiling?
faq.a: Melting is the change from a solid to a liquid. Boiling is the change from a liquid to a gas.
asks: When does a solid become a liquid?
What process changes ice to water?

faq.q: Do gases have particles at all?
faq.a: Yes, gases are made of particles, but they are very far apart. These particles move very quickly.
asks: What is the particle movement in a gas?

faq.q: Can matter change back and forth between states?
faq.a: Yes, matter can change between all three states. For example, water can freeze or evaporate.
asks: What happens when steam cools down?

faq.q: What causes matter to change its state?
faq.a: Adding or removing heat energy causes the particles to move faster or slower. This changes the state.
Yes, even in a solid, the particles are always vibrating in place. They never stop moving.
asks: Is particle movement only in liquids and gases?

facts: Solids have a definite shape and definite volume.
Liquids have a definite volume but take the shape of their container.
Gases have neither a definite shape nor a definite volume.
Melting is the change from solid to liquid.
Boiling is the change from liquid to gas.

quiz.say: Which state of matter has particles packed very closely together and vibrates in place?
quiz.why: In a solid, the particles are locked into place and can only vibrate.

wrong.1: Liquids are more spread out and can slide past each other.
wrong.2: Gases have particles that are very far apart from each other.
wrong.3: Plasma is another state, but we are only learning about the three main ones.

quiz.say: When water boils, what is happening to its particles?

options.show: They slow down and stick together.
options.say: They slow down and stick together.

options.show: They just vibrate a little bit.
options.say: They just vibrate a little bit.

options.show: They move very fast and spread out.
options.say: They move very fast and spread out.

quiz.why: Boiling gives the particles enough energy to escape as a gas.

wrong.0: Slowing down happens when the substance cools down.
wrong.1: Vibration is what happens in a solid, not boiling.
wrong.2: Boiling is a change of state, not just a shape change.

quiz.say: If you leave an ice cube outside, what is the first change you observe?

options.show: It gets harder to the touch.
options.say: It gets harder to the touch.

quiz.why: The solid ice absorbs heat and changes into the liquid state.

wrong.0: Matter cannot just disappear; it changes form.
wrong.1: Melting makes it softer, not harder.
wrong.3: That would require a very high amount of heat energy.
